note: Transit events (S3.3, D-111; brief §15), situations aboard since H.7 (D-156, D-200): each says where it happens (`place`: a room of the ship, or "radio"), what is known before anyone is there (`sign`), and what comes of leaving it alone (`lapse`). The format is described at the top of src/narrative/events.js, conditions in src/narrative/conditions.js, effects in src/narrative/effects.js. These first ten show every part of the format at work; S3.5 brings the count to 30.

items.title: {place}: {hazard}
items.sign: The lane ahead runs straight through {hazard}. I would like somebody on the bridge before it does.

lapse.text: Nobody took her through {hazard} by hand. Something the size of a fist goes through the outer skin and keeps going.

items.text: The lane runs straight through {hazard}. The chart, last updated by a company that no longer exists, calls it navigable. The hull has started to tick.

choices.label: Hold the course and take what comes

outcomes.text: It is loud for four minutes and then it is not. Nothing you can find is broken.
Something the size of a fist goes through the outer skin and keeps going. The ship is a little less of a ship than it was.
A surge comes up through the frame and finds the sensor mast. One bar of it is slag.

choices.label: Slow to a crawl and sweep ahead

outcomes.text: The sensors pick a way through, one clear pocket at a time. It costs the better part of a watch you had been counting on.

choices.label: Let the best hands aboard fly it

outcomes.text: {pilot} takes the helm and does not speak for twenty minutes. When it is over there is not a mark on the hull, and {pilot} needs a moment before standing up.

items.title: A dead hull at {place}
items.sign: A dead hull, close alongside. No lights, no transponder. I have hove us to; somebody could look it over from the lock in {room}.

lapse.text: Nobody goes to the lock. The dead hull drops astern, still turning, and we are under way again.

items.text: A freighter of the old company pattern turns slowly off the lock. No lights, no transponder, one airlock standing open. {who} is already looking at it the way people look at an unlocked door.

choices.label: Leave it turning

outcomes.text: You log the position and go on. Whatever is in there stays in there.

choices.label: Send {who} across with a line and a lamp

outcomes.text: {who} comes back with a crate under one arm and frost on the faceplate. "Galley's intact. Somebody set the table." There is a strongbox too.

effects.label: Salvage from a dead hull
effects.contents: Sealed ration tins, a kettle, and a table setting for six, wrapped in a company-issue blanket.

outcomes.text: A deck plate lets go under {who} two compartments in. The line holds. The leg mostly holds. Nothing comes back but {who}.
{who} is back early and seals the lock by hand. "There's a log on the bridge. You should hear it before we go anywhere."

choices.label: Have an engineer cut the fuel cell out

outcomes.text: {cutter} is across and back inside the hour, towing a cell with the old company's stencil still on it. It reads a third full, which is a third more than it had any right to.
{cutter} gets the cell out clean, and then there is nowhere to put it. The tanks are full. It goes back out of the lock, still worth something to somebody.

items.title: The last entry
items.sign: The log from the dead hull is on the bridge console. Somebody should hear it before we go anywhere.

lapse.text: The recording sat unplayed on the bridge for most of a watch. I have filed it under its manifest number, and I will not say anything about the number.

items.text: The recording is eleven seconds long. A woman reads a manifest number twice, slowly, the way you read something to a person who is not listening. Then a door closes somewhere behind her and she stops reading.

choices.label: Keep the recording

outcomes.text: Margo files it under the manifest number. She does not say anything about the number, and you notice that she does not.

effects.text: A dead freighter at {place} logged a manifest number twice before the recording stopped.

choices.label: Wipe it and go

outcomes.text: It is gone. The crew are quieter than they were an hour ago.
It is gone. That night there is a sound in the crawlway that the pumps do not account for, and nobody mentions it at breakfast.

items.title: Patrol line at {place}
items.text: A cutter with fresh paint over an old company crest holds the lane. The voice on the channel is young, bored, and reading from a card. It wants your manifest, your registry, and a transit fee that was not on any chart.

choices.label: Send the manifest and wait

outcomes.text: A long pause. "Proceed." The card evidently had nothing more on it.
"There is a discrepancy fee." There is no discrepancy. There is a fee.

choices.label: Pay the fee and keep the receipt

outcomes.text: The receipt is stamped with a seal belonging to an office that closed nine years ago. They wave you through before you can read the rest.

choices.label: Put someone on the channel who can talk

outcomes.text: {voice} asks the officer's name, then the officer's captain's name, then whether the captain knows about the fee. The lane is clear in under a minute.
{voice} pushes one question too far. The channel goes quiet, and then the cutter's guns come round.

choices.label: Say nothing and burn through the line

outcomes.text: They were not expecting it. By the time anyone on that cutter has put down a cup, you are a heat trace and a bad report.
They were expecting it. The cutter is already turning.

items.title: A beacon in the dark
items.sign: A distress beacon, low power, four minutes off the lane. It is on the scope. Whoever goes to {room} can decide what we do about it.

lapse.text: Nobody answered the beacon. It repeats itself behind us until the range opens and it is only noise.

items.text: A distress beacon, low power, repeating a ship's name nobody aboard recognises. It is four minutes off the lane. Beacons in the Reach are sometimes what they say they are.

choices.label: Log it and pass by

outcomes.text: The beacon repeats itself behind you until the range opens and it is only noise.

choices.label: Answer it

outcomes.text: A lifeboat, long empty, its locker still sealed. Somebody packed it for a fight they did not get to have.
The beacon is bolted to a rock. The skiff behind the rock has been waiting some time.
By the time you match the drift the beacon has stopped. There is nothing on the sensors, and there was nothing on them before.

choices.label: Hold off and listen first

requires.label: A trained hand on the sensors

outcomes.text: With the gain up there is a second signature tucked in behind the beacon: a small drive, banked low and warm. You leave it sitting there.

effects.text: Somebody is using a false beacon near {place}.

items.title: {patient} has a cough
items.sign: {patient} has had a cough since the last port and has stopped pretending otherwise. Somebody else should look in at {room}.

lapse.text: Nobody looked in on {patient}. The cough has gone down onto the chest.

items.text: {patient} has had a cough since the last port and has stopped pretending otherwise. It is probably the scrubbers. On this ship it is usually the scrubbers.

choices.label: Tell {patient} to sleep it off

outcomes.text: A day in a bunk does what a day in a bunk does. The cough moves on.
It is not the scrubbers. {patient} is grey by the next watch and angry about being asked.

choices.label: Have someone who knows medicine take a look

outcomes.text: {medic} listens to {patient}'s chest for a long time, says a word nobody else knows, and comes back from the medbay with something that works.

choices.label: Stop the air plant and strip the scrubbers

outcomes.text: The filter that comes out is the colour of the inside of a chimney. The new one is the last new one.

items.title: Somebody's wake
items.sign: There is a trace on the bridge monitor I think somebody should see. It is a drive signature, and it is not ours.

lapse.text: The trace stays on the bridge monitor a while and then scrolls off. Whoever it is, they are still back there.

items.text: Margo puts a trace on the monitor without being asked: a drive signature, hours old, laid over your own track like a second line of handwriting. Whoever it is, they are not in a hurry.

choices.label: Note it and keep moving

outcomes.text: You keep moving. The trace stays on the monitor a little longer than it needs to.

choices.label: Vent the drive plume and cut a false trail

outcomes.text: Two units of fuel go out as a bright smear pointing the wrong way. It should cost whoever is back there a good few hours working out which line is yours.

items.title: Something in the hold
items.sign: Something moved in {room}, behind the crates. It is warm, it is breathing, and it is not on my crew list.

lapse.text: Nobody went down to look. By the next watch the galley is two ration tins short and the hold is quiet again.

items.text: {who} finds a boy of about fifteen wedged in behind the machine parts with a water flask and a company blanket. He says he came aboard at the last port, that he can work, and that he would rather not say why he left.

choices.label: Put him to work until the next port

outcomes.text: He scrubs filters for two watches without being asked twice, and sleeps on the sacking by the lift. The air plant has not smelled this clean since the second owner.
He works. The medical crate is also a blister pack lighter by morning, and he swears it was like that when he found it.

choices.label: Lock him in the brig until port

outcomes.text: He goes quietly, which is somehow worse. {who} leaves him the blanket.

choices.label: Have someone find out who he is running from

outcomes.text: {voice} sits on a crate and waits him out. It takes most of an hour. The Receivers are paying for names off the dock lists, and his father's was on one.

effects.text: A stowaway says the Receivers are paying for names off the dock lists.

items.title: A crate is leaking
items.sign: Something is dripping in {room}. The deck sensor calls it coolant. I do not think it is coolant.

lapse.text: Nobody went to look at the drip in {room}. It has found something it can burn.

items.text: {who} follows the drip to one of the manifest crates. The seal has gone along one edge and something pale is beading out of it, slowly, taking the paint off the deck where it lands.

choices.label: Wrap it in sealant tape and leave it be

outcomes.text: {who} uses most of a roll. The drip stops. The crate sits there looking no different from the others, which is the idea.
The tape holds for an hour. Then the deck plate under the crate lets go at one corner, and there is a whistle in {room} that was not there before.

choices.label: Have an engineer reseal it properly

outcomes.text: {fixer} cuts the old seal out, swears at whoever packed it, and lays a new bead. The manifest says machine parts. {fixer} says nothing, loudly.

choices.label: Open it and see what is leaking

outcomes.text: Battery cells, old ones, packed wet. {who} gets the lid back on with a burned glove and a new opinion of the client.

effects.text: One of the manifest crates is full of wet-packed battery cells nobody declared.

outcomes.text: The lid comes off and the air gets at whatever it is. {who} is out of the way in time. The crate is not.

items.title: {first} and {second} are fighting
items.sign: Raised voices in {room}. {first} and {second}. It has gone past words, and I do not have hands.

lapse.text: Nobody came. {first} and {second} finished it themselves, and both of them are bleeding.

items.text: {who} finds them in {room}: {first} has {second} against the bulkhead by the collar. Neither will say what it was about. There is a broken mug on the deck and it was somebody's only mug.

choices.label: Get between them

outcomes.text: It takes a shoulder and a loud voice. {first} lets go. They sit at opposite ends of the table and do not look up.
{who} gets between them and takes the elbow that was meant for somebody else. It ends it, at least.

choices.label: Let them finish it

outcomes.text: It lasts under a minute, the way real ones do. Afterwards {second} picks up the pieces of the mug.

choices.label: Have someone talk them down

outcomes.text: {voice} asks which of them wants to explain it to the captain, and waits. It turns out neither does.

items.title: A load adrift in the hold
items.sign: Something in {room} has come off its straps. I can hear it from here, and so, I would think, can anyone listening.

lapse.text: Nobody went down. The load rolled until it found the hull plating, and the plating gave a little.

items.text: {who} gets to {room} as a pallet of machine parts slides the width of the deck and fetches up against the bulkhead with a sound like a bell. The strap that held it is lying in two pieces.

choices.label: Get a line on it and lash it down

outcomes.text: {who} waits for the roll, gets a line round it on the way back, and hauls. It stops. It is very quiet in {room} afterwards.
It stops, eventually, against {who}'s shin. The line holds. The shin mostly holds.

choices.label: Wedge it with whatever is to hand

outcomes.text: Two ration crates and a spare door seal. It will not move again until somebody needs the ration crates.

items.title: The reactor is knocking
items.sign: That round rang the reactor housing. A coolant line in {room} has started knocking, and it is running hot.

lapse.text: Nobody went to the reactor. The knocking stopped on its own, which is when the line split.

items.text: {who} finds the line jumping against its bracket with every pulse of the pump. The lagging is smoking where it touches the housing.

choices.label: Have an engineer bleed the line

outcomes.text: {fixer} cracks the bleed valve, lets the air out of the line in one long hiss, and the knocking stops dead. "Somebody packed this with a bubble in it," {fixer} says. "Somebody I would like to meet."

choices.label: Clamp it to the bracket and hope

outcomes.text: {who} clamps it with a spanner and a strap. The knocking becomes a shiver. The shiver is quieter.
The clamp holds the line still and the heat goes somewhere else instead: a seam weeps coolant onto the deck, and {who} pulls back a scalded hand.

items.title: The sensor head is howling
items.sign: Their ping came in hot and our sensor head in {room} is howling it back. It is telling them where we are, a little at a time.

lapse.text: Nobody went to the sensors. The howl went on until something in the head burned out, and then it stopped.

items.text: {who} finds the sensor head's amplifier feeding back on itself: a whine you feel in your teeth and a panel too hot to touch.

choices.label: Pull the head's fuse

outcomes.text: The whine stops at once, and so does the head. We are blind on that side until somebody puts it back together.

choices.label: Have someone who knows sensors damp it by hand

outcomes.text: {tech} finds the loop, pulls one card a finger's width out of its slot, and the howl drops to a hum. "Leave that card alone," {tech} says to nobody in particular.

choices.label: Let it ring itself out

outcomes.text: It rings itself out. It takes four very long minutes.
It rings itself out, and takes the amplifier with it.

items.title: {shaky} has lost their nerve
items.sign: {shaky} heard that through the deck. They are in {room}, and they are not being quiet about it.

lapse.text: Nobody went to {shaky}. They wore themselves out in the end. They will not look at the scope now.

items.text: {who} finds {shaky} in {room} with their back to the bulkhead, talking too fast and too loud about the last ship that pinged a hauler, and what was left of the hauler.

choices.label: Sit with them until it passes

outcomes.text: {who} sits down beside {shaky} and says nothing much for ten minutes. It is the right amount of nothing.

choices.label: Tell them to keep it down

outcomes.text: {shaky} keeps it down. {shaky} also keeps a note of who said it.

choices.label: Have a medic give them something

outcomes.text: {medic} gets something from the medbay into {shaky} and a blanket round them. They are asleep inside the quarter hour.

items.title: The stowaway is beating on the brig door
items.sign: The boy in {room} has worked out what a ping means. He is beating on the door with both fists.

lapse.text: Nobody went to the brig. He got the lock open with the blanket's buckle. He is somewhere aboard.

items.text: {who} opens the hatch on a boy with split knuckles and a white face. "They find stowaways," he says. "They find stowaways and they take the ship."

choices.label: Tell him what is out there, and that he is safer quiet

outcomes.text: {who} tells him, plainly. He sits down on the bunk and puts his hands under his arms and does not make another sound.
{who} tells him. It does not help. He goes on, quieter, which will have to do.

choices.label: Let him out to help

outcomes.text: He is out of the brig and holding a lamp for {who} inside a minute, and he does not say a word the whole time.

items.title: A slug loose in the gun room
items.sign: That warning shot shook a slug out of its cradle in {room}. It is rolling, and it is heavy.

lapse.text: Nobody went to the gun room. The slug found the feed and jammed it.

items.text: {who} finds a slug the length of a forearm trundling across {room}, ringing off the racks every time the ship rolls.

choices.label: Catch it and rack it

outcomes.text: {who} times it, catches it on the bounce, and seats it back in the cradle with a kick.
{who} catches it. It catches {who} first, across the knuckles.

choices.label: Put it out of the lock

outcomes.text: Out it goes. One slug fewer, and one less thing rolling about in the dark.
